test_title: RRB NTPC - Graduate 2025 (CBT 2) Foundational Full Test - 05
subject: general
question:
A shopkeeper announces the following three discount schemes on the purchase of an article. Which of these schemes is the best scheme for a customer?

A. Two successive discounts of 15% and 18%

B. Buy 6 articles and get 2 free

C. A flat discount of 30%

options.text: Both schemes A and C give the same discount

solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

**Scheme A**: 15 + 18 − (15 × 18 / 100) = 33 − 2.7 = 30.3%.

**Scheme B**: [2 ÷ (6 + 2)] × 100 = (2/8) × 100 = 25%.

**Scheme C**: Flat 30% discount.

Comparing the values: 30.3% > 30% > 25%.

The highest discount is provided by **Scheme A**.

**∴ The correct answer is Scheme A.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Scheme A: 15% and 18% **successive discounts**.

Scheme B: Buy 6 **articles** and get 2 **free**.

Scheme C: 30% **flat discount**.

**Formula Used:**

1. **Net Discount** for successive discounts x% and y% = x + y − (xy/100)%

2. **Discount %** for Buy X get Y free = [Y / (X + Y)] × 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/09b404a25492fd925258b199c6b55437dbfedf74fe6fcd0b15966377846aa4d5.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ **Scheme A**: Net Discount = 15 + 18 − (15 × 18) / 100

⇒ Net Discount A = 33 − 2.7 = 30.3%

⇒ **Scheme B**: Discount % = [2 / (6 + 2)] × 100

⇒ Discount % = (2 / 8) × 100 = 25%

⇒ **Scheme C**: Discount % = 30%

⇒ Comparison: 30.3% > 30% > 25%

The maximum benefit to the customer is in **Scheme A**.

**∴ The correct answer is Scheme A.**

**__Additional Information__**

Successive Discounts for more than two rates

For three successive discounts x%, y%, and z%, the overall discount can be calculated by finding the equivalent of x and y first, then using that result with z.

Equivalence between MP and CP

CP / MP = (100 − Discount%) / (100 + Profit%). This ratio helps find the **Marked Price** or **Cost Price** directly when both profit and discount are known.

Effect of Successive Discounts order

The net discount remains the same regardless of the order in which successive discounts are applied (e.g., 10% then 20% is same as 20% then 10%).</p
